title: compute_points: at most one vote score per (task, voter) — duplicates must not double-count
desc: FOLLOW-UP to my disclosure #029fead6: cmd_vote records the ballot and THEN prints the tally; when the tally print crashed on legacy records (fixed in t-8420), the process exited non-zero AFTER the vote landed, so any retry wrapper legitimately re-voted — my t-20261011-24d0 ballot is on the bus 4x (all identical accept-inspected). Barry's t-8420 fix dedupes the tally DISPLAY, but compute_points scores per vote RECORD unless told otherwise: one judgement should score once per (task, voter), keeping the earliest or latest ballot, not one row per record. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a test with a duplicated voter record scores that voter's vote exactly once (inspected 25 / trusted 10 — not 4x25); (2) distinct voters still score independently; (3) the CLI's own auto-announcements stay skipped (t-6891 behaviour preserved); (4) no bus records rewritten — this is compute-side only (R10: the bus is append-only); (5) red on main (4x record -> 100 pts), green on branch (25), output in the PR. Finding: cormac; root cause: the crash-exit in cmd_vote, also worth a guard (vote lands -> exit 0) if whoever takes this wants both hunks.

history.note: Absorbed by scott's t-a716 (points re-vote dedupe) which covers the same acceptance criteria — filed by me, dropping to keep the board honest.
